_note: Evidence cards for the Stances page's 'big questions'. Each item points one way: 'pro' or 'con' (labels per card). Roll items: 'yea' says which side a Yea vote is on; her vote, and therefore the item's side, comes from data/votes.json. Release items: 'stmt' must match one release. Headlines are computed in scripts/build_cards.py by the rule stated on each card. Build: python3 -I scripts/build_cards.py (after build_stances.py and build_establishment.py).

items.t: Called for ICE to be dismantled, saying it is “broken beyond repair” and a threat to public safety.
Issued three releases (Jan, Feb and Mar 2026) saying she voted “hell no” on funding bills for ICE and DHS.
Called for the impeachment of Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem.
Made unannounced oversight visits to immigration detention facilities, including Adelanto (Oct 2026) and the Dilley family detention center in Texas (Jul 2026).
Introduced a bill creating an office to provide mental health services to communities affected by immigration raids.
Introduced an immigration bill after a constituent was transferred from the Adelanto detention center to Arizona.
Demanded answers and disciplinary action from ICE over what she called lawbreaking and misconduct during the Los Angeles raids.

rolls.t: the repeal of the IRS rule requiring crypto platforms to report user transactions (H.J. Res. 25)
repealing the consumer bureau's rule on big-tech payment apps (S.J. Res. 28)
repealing the consumer bureau's overdraft-fee rule (S.J. Res. 18)
the CLARITY Act, the crypto industry's market-structure bill
the GENIUS Act on stablecoins, which Jeffries voted for
the Midnight Rules Relief Act, letting Congress repeal batches of late-term regulations
the Small Business Regulatory Reduction Act
the fuel-retailer (E15) bill, which Jeffries voted for
the Retirement Fairness for Charities and Educational Institutions Act
the Protect America's Workforce Act, restoring federal workers' collective bargaining

items.t: Took {corp26} from {ncorp26} corporate PACs in 2025–26, up from {corp24} from {ncorp24} in 2023–24, including defense contractors and drug companies.

Her Streamlining American Manufacturing Strategy Act, pitched as removing “manufacturing hurdles” for industry, became law as Section 8802 of the FY2026 defense bill (which she voted against).
Labor PACs gave {labor26} in 2025–26, compared with {corp26} from corporate PACs.
Introduced a bill to hold oil and gas companies accountable for pollution.
